U.S. added stronger than expected 162,000 jobs in August as labor market bounced back
items.article_summary: "What a 'wow' jobs report," said Heather Long, the chief economist at the Navy Federal Credit Union, in an email. Although job creation accelerated in August, wage growth remained sluggish at 3.1%, the lowest since May 2021. "If those come in cooler than expected, the Fed will likely feel comfortable discounting potentially inflationary signals coming out of the labor market." Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh affirmed that the labor market was on a steady course last week during the Fed's annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. "In general, though, people who want to work, by and large, are holding or finding jobs." Warsh signaled that inflation, which is stubbornly above the Fed's 2% target, remains the central bank's primary focus.

IMF confirms El Salvador’s bitcoin growth was funded by private donations, not public money
items.article_summary: Private donations account for the Bitcoin El Salvador has added to its national reserve since mid-2025, the International Monetary Fund said on Thursday, announcing a staff-level agreement on the country's combined second and third program reviews. In September 2025, an IMF communications officer told Decrypt that the total quantity of government-owned Bitcoin had not increased at all, and that growth in El Salvador's Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Fund reflected coins moving between wallets the state already controlled. The reserve held 5,968 BTC when the program began in December 2024 and now stands at 7,764 BTC, per El Salvador's Bitcoin Office. As recently as last week, the Bitcoin Office tweeted that El Salvador had "just bought more Bitcoin," attaching a treasury chart showing 31 coins added over 30 days, contradicting the IMF's account.

items.title: U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, July 2026
items.article_summary: Bureau of Economic Analysis announced today that the goods and services deficit was $88.6 billion in July, up $17.4 billion from $71.2 billion in June, revised. July imports were $399.3 billion, $10.8 billion more than June imports. The July increase in the goods and services deficit reflected an increase in the goods deficit of $17.6 billion to $119.6 billion and an increase in the services surplus of $0.2 billion to $31.0 billion. Year-to-date, the goods and services deficit decreased $188.4 billion, or 29.6 percent, from the same period in 2025.
items.article_context: Bureau of Economic Analysis announced today that the goods and services deficit was $88.6 billion in July, up $17.4 billion from $71.2 billion in June, revised. (°) Statistical significance is not applicable or not measurable. Data adjusted for seasonality but not price changes Source: U.S. July imports were $399.3 billion, $10.8 billion more than June imports. The July increase in the goods and services deficit reflected an increase in the goods deficit of $17.6 billion to $119.6 billion and an increase in the services surplus of $0.2 billion to $31.0 billion. Year-to-date, the goods and services deficit decreased $188.4 billion, or 29.6 percent, from the same period in 2025. Exports increased $237.2 billion or 12.0 percent. Imports increased $48.8 billion or 1.9 percent. The average goods and services deficit increased $11.9 billion to $78.5 billion for the three months ending in July. Year-over-year, the average goods and services deficit increased $11.7 billion from the three months ending in July 2025. Exports of goods decreased $6.2 billion to $201.0 billion in July. Exports of goods on a Census basis decreased $5.9 billion. Net balance of payments adjustments decreased $0.3 billion. When incorporating the statistics in this release into BEA’s National Economic Accounts, including Gross Domestic Product, or GDP, BEA replaces exports and imports of nonmonetary gold with an adjustment calculated as the difference between domestic production and industrial use of gold.
